newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. envoy, HK's Tung toast American independence.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy, HK's Tung toast American independence.

text.p: New Hong Kong leader Tung Chee-hwa and U.S. Consul General Richard Boucher joked and toasted American independence day on Friday at a reception packed with the business community's high and mighty.
With the American and Chinese flags side by side, Boucher said Tung was "a man in whom we have great hope and confidence".
Tung lived and worked in the United States. His three children were born there and have U.S. passports.
Handpicked by Communist China, Tung took over as Hong Kong's chief executive on Tuesday when more than 150 years of British rule came to an end.
Under terms of a 1984 agreement, Hong Kong is to remain a largely autonomous region of China for the next 50 years and be allowed to keep its super-capitalist ways.
"So from now on the United States and Hong Kong will celebrate similar anniversaries during the first week of July," Boucher said at the reception at his residence.
"I don't think they'll call theirs independence day, though," he quipped.
Tung, who must play a delicate role between Beijing and the capitalist world, did not join in the general laughter.
As guest of honour, Tung returned the toast by saying that the United States "is a very important partner for Hong Kong, in terms of people, trade and culture".
He said his aim would be "to enhance this relationship as we move into the 21st century".
